questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It mainly was the courses offered at the Exchange-University. I was very interested in ecosystems other than the European ones.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. The University of Melbourne hosted an orientation day for exchange students prior to a full orientation week for all students and provided a lot of information and help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: How to get my public transport card, assistance with extra curricular activities, assistance with finances.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing market in Melbourne is pretty hard, almost equal to Copenhagen. I would recommend Facebook sites, especially Fairy Floss Real Estate. Also: The housing market is quite short-notice, so don't be discouraged if you haven't found anything two months before your departure.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The commute can be quite long, as the city is huge. Try to find something close to the University if possible. Also: Most houses do not have good insulation, so be prepared for a cold winter.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't be afraid of the traffic; biking pays off here too.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I do not remember all of it, but there was a step-to-step guide on their website available.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The University provides all sorts of help. You can email them with any questions. There is also a step-to-step guide for registration. When your application is accepted, they send you further information and links in an email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got everything I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start as soon as possible, like always.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were of very mixed quality.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Most of the courses are mixed Bachelor's and Master's courses, and the demands are not adjusted to your level. 
While some Professors were very engaging and encouraging, others seemed to lack enthusiasm.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style is quite similar. The classes are small, and everything is quite interactive, with the Professors and Lecturers encouraging discussion and being on eye level with the students. However, the assignment process is a little different. While most of the grade is based on one big assignment at the end of the Block or Semester in CPH, the courses in Melbourne have a lot of small assignments during the semester, which requires the students to work on the course constantly. With a full study load, that can get quite challenging. Also, it is mainly written assignments, hardly any oral exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Nature, Conservation and Society 10/10
Economic Tools for the Environment  2/10
Science Communication  9/10
Communities and Ecosystem Management  5/10

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Nature, Conservation and Society and Science Communication. 
The Professor running NCS is enthusiastic, and her teaching style in the tutorials is excellent. We had many fruitful discussions, and the topics and assignments helped develop a deeper understanding of conservation. 
Although Science Communication is rather demanding because of the many assignments to hand in over the semester, it is worth it. You get an excellent insight into the different communication perspectives and can try out many things yourself. There are also fascinating people on the course, both fellow students and lecturers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Public transport is quite expensive, and so is local produce at some times of the year. Alcohol and going out are also astonishingly expensive. Joining sport clubs is also not cheap, but that's the same in CPH

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol is way more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many social clubs and sports to choose from.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything, from language clubs to film clubs, food clubs and all sorts of things. A lot of sports clubs, too. You can also enter volleyball and football tournaments, that go the whole semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Exchange-student society was good for getting in contact with other exchange students. The film society shows a movie every Friday with free pizza. Just browse through the social clubs, I bet you find something that is in your interest.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get out of the city. Go to Tasmania (at least a week), Phillip Island, Wilsons Prom, the Grampians, and Great Ocean Road. Also: Ruffey Trail Suspension Bridge in the early morning or evening if you want to spot some platypuses.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, it's just another western culture. But Melbourne is very diverse with many different nationalities coming together. Very interesting

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the social clubs and sport events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very friendly and curious

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go to the social clubs
Be prepared for bad weather
Enjoy your life, don't worry too much about your grades

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Travelling the country and seeing all this amazing wildlife

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Facing the cold without a heater in my room

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
